facts.text: During the Second World War the Indian freedom struggle became more extensive, and the British began preparing plans for granting Independence to India.
facts.quote: During the period of Second World War, Indian freedom struggle had become more extensive. ... Accordingly, the British government started preparing various plans for granting Independence to India.

facts.text: The Indian National Congress was founded on the principle of secularism; people of all caste and religion took part in the national struggle.
facts.quote: The Indian National Congress was founded on the principle of secularism. People of all caste and religion had taken part in the national struggle.

facts.text: To weaken the movement the British adopted the policy of 'divide and rule'; its consequence was the establishment of the 'Muslim League'.
facts.quote: To weaken this movement the British adopted the policy of 'divide and rule'. Its consequence was the establishment of 'Muslim League'.

facts.text: In 1930 Dr. Muhammad Iqbal, a well known poet, put forth the thought of an independent Muslim state.
facts.quote: In 1930, Dr. Muhammad Iqbal, a well known poet, put forth the thought of an independent Muslim state.

facts.text: Later Chaudhary Rahmat Ali put up the idea of Pakistan.
facts.quote: Later Chaudhary Rahmat Ali put up the idea of Pakistan.

facts.text: Barrister Muhammad Ali Jinnah put forth the two Nation theory and demanded a separate Muslim nation named Pakistan.
facts.quote: Barrister Muhammad Ali Jinnah put forth the two Nation theory and demanded a seperate Muslim nation named Pakistan.

facts.text: Barrister Jinnah and the Muslim League spread propaganda that the Congress was only a Hindu organisation.
facts.quote: Indian National Congress was only a Hindu organisation, the muslims have no benefit of it; such kind of propaganda was started by Barrister Jinnah and the Muslim League.

facts.text: In June 1945 Lord Wavell, the Viceroy of India, drew up a plan.
facts.quote: In June 1945, Lord Wavell, the Viceroy of India drew up a plan.

facts.text: The Wavell Plan proposed proper representation for Muslims, Dalits and minorities in the legislatures and an equal number of Hindu and Muslim members in the Viceroy's Executive Council.
facts.quote: in central and provincial legislatures Muslims, Dalits and minorities should be given proper representation and there will be equal number of Hindu and Muslim members in Viceroy's Executive Council.

facts.text: A meeting of all major political parties was organised at Simla to consider the Wavell Plan.
facts.quote: A meeting of all major political parties in India was organised at Simla to consider the Wavell Plan.

facts.text: Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League should suggest the Muslim names for the Viceroy's Executive Council; the Congress opposed it, so the Wavell Plan failed.
facts.quote: Barrister Jinnah insisted that only the Muslim League should have the right to suggest the names of muslim representatives to the Viceroy's Executive Council. But the Congress opposed it. Therefore the Wavell plan could not be successful.

facts.text: After the Second World War, British Prime Minister Attlee recognised the right of Indian people to draft their own Constitution and said the minorities issue would not block India's Independence.
facts.quote: In the Parliament, British Prime Minister Attlee clarified the British policy regarding India. According to it, the right of Indian people to draft their own Constitution was recognised. It was also made clear that the issue of minorities will not come in the way of India's Independence.

facts.text: In March 1946 British ministers Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander put England's plan before Indian leaders; this is called the 'Cabinet Mission'.
facts.quote: In March 1946, a delegation of British ministers namely Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander put forth England's plan regarding India in front of the Indian leaders. This is called 'Cabinet Mission'.

facts.text: Some provisions of the Cabinet Mission were not acceptable to the Congress, and the Muslim League was unsatisfied as there was no independent state for the muslims; so it was not fully accepted.
facts.quote: Some of the provision in the plan were not acceptable to the Congress. Similarly, there was no provision of independent state for the muslims, so the Muslim League was unsatisfied. Therefore Cabinet Mission was not fully accepted.

facts.text: Since the demand for Pakistan was not fulfilled, the Muslim League declared 16 August 1946 as 'Direct Action Day'.
facts.quote: Accordingly, 16 August 1946, was declared to be observed as 'Direct Action Day' by the Muslim League.

facts.text: There were Hindu-Muslim riots in various parts of the country and massacres in the Noakhali region in the province of Bengal; Gandhiji went there without thinking of his own life to establish peace.
facts.quote: There were Hindu-Muslim riots in various parts of the country. There were massacres in the Noakhali region in the province of Bengal. To stop this violence Gandhiji went there without giving any thought to his own life. He tried his best to establish peace there.

facts.text: Viceroy Wavell established the Interim Government; Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was its head.
facts.quote: Viceroy Wavell established the Interim Government. Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was the head of this government.

facts.text: The Muslim League first refused to join the Interim Government but later joined; its policy of obstruction stopped the government working smoothly.
facts.quote: The Muslim League initially denied to participate in the Interim Government, but later, participated in it. But since the leaders of Muslim League adopted the policy of obstruction, hence the Interim Government could not work smoothly.

facts.text: Prime Minister Atlee announced that England would leave its dominion on India before June 1948.
facts.quote: England's Prime Minister Atlee had announced that England would leave its dominion on India before June 1948.

facts.text: Lord Mountbatten was appointed Viceroy; after talks with Indian leaders he prepared a plan to create India and Pakistan as two independent nations.
facts.quote: Lord Mountbatten was appointed as Viceroy of India. Mountbatten held discussions with prominent leaders of India. Thereafter, he prepared a plan of creation of India and Pakistan as two independent nations.

facts.text: The Congress opposed partition, as unity of the nation was its basic stand, but the Muslim League stayed adamant; the Congress accepted partition with complete helplessness.
facts.quote: Indian National Congress opposed the plan of partition. Unity of the nation, was the basic stand of Indian National Congress, but the Muslim League remained adamant on the creation of Pakistan. National Congress was left with no option but to accept the decision of partition with complete helplessness.

facts.text: On 18 July 1947, on the basis of the Mountbatten Plan, the Indian Independence Act was passed in the British Parliament.
facts.quote: On 18 July 1947, on the basis of Mountbatten Plan, the Indian Independence Act was passed in British Parliament.

facts.text: Under the Act, India and Pakistan would come into existence on 15 August 1947; the British Parliament would have no control over them, British supremacy over the princely states would end, and the princely states could join India or Pakistan or remain independent.
facts.quote: On 15 August 1947, the two independent nations India and Pakistan will come into existence. Thereafter the British Parliament will not have any control over them. The British supremacy over the princely states will also come to an end. The Act provided them the right to either join India or Pakistan or remain independent.

facts.text: As per the Indian Independence Act, India was granted independence on 15 August 1947.
facts.quote: As per the Indian Independence Act, India was granted independence on 15 August 1947.

facts.text: A meeting of the Constituent Assembly was going on in the hall of Parliament House in Delhi at midnight of 14 August 1947; the Union Jack was lowered and the Indian tricolour flag was unfurled.
facts.quote: A meeting of the Constituent Assembly was going on in the hall of Parliament House in Delhi in the midnight of 14 August 1947. At the stroke of midnight hour, India's dependence came to an end. The Union Jack of Britain was lowered and in its place the Indian tricolour flag was unfurled.

facts.text: India attained Independence from 150 years of slavery.
facts.quote: India attained Independence from the 150 years of slavery.

facts.text: People were grieved by partition and terrible violence; instead of joining the celebration, Gandhiji was striving hard in Bengal.
facts.quote: Indian people were grieved due to the partition of the country and the terrible violence during that period. Instead of joining the celebration of Independence, Gandhiji was striving hard in Bengal.

facts.text: Within six months of freedom, Gandhiji was assassinated by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948.
facts.quote: Within six months of attainment of freedom of India, Gandhiji was brutally assassinated by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948.

facts.text: Gandhiji strove day and night to preserve Hindu Muslim unity and laid down his life for it.
facts.quote: Gandhiji strove day and night to preserve Hindu Muslim unity and laid down his life for the same.

facts.text: The map 'Independent India 15th August 1947' shows Pakistan in two parts, West Pakistan and East Pakistan.
facts.quote: Independent India 15th August 1947 ... WEST PAKISTAN ... EAST PAKISTAN

facts.text: On that map Goa, Diu, Daman and Dadra and Nagar Haveli are marked Portuguese, while Puduchcheri, Karikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandranagar are marked French.
facts.quote: Goa (Portuguese) ... Diu ... Daman (Portuguese) ... Dadra and Nagar Haveli (Portuguese) ... Puduchcheri (Pondicherry) ... Karikal (French) ... Mahe (French) ... Yanam (French) ... Chandranagar (French)
